source_text: Maximianus quidam diaconus fuit Carthaginiensis in parte Donati. siue merito superbiae suae siue, ut ipsi putant, merito iustitiae suae offendit episcopum suum, id est Primianum Carthaginiensem, siue inique, si superbus meliorem, siue iuste, si probus inprobiorem. excommunicatus est a Primiano. perrexit ad episcopos uicinos, concitauit inuidiam Primiano, accusauit eum apud illos. uentum est ad Carthaginem. uoluerunt qui uenerunt multi episcopi Donatistae ad se uenire Primianum, sicut uoluerunt maiores istorum ad se uenire Caecilianum. factione cognita noluit ad istos uenire Primianus, sicut ad illos noluit uenire Caecilianus. damnatus est ab istis absens Primianus, sicut ab illis damnatus est absens Caecilianus. qualem imaginem rerum uoluit deus ante oculos nostros recenti tempore ponere, quoniam nimis antiqua iam delebat obliuio! damnatus est absens. ab aliis episcopis partis Donati Primianus communioni est restitutus, immo quia eum non deposuerunt, in sua sede firmatus est. damnati sunt Maximianistae, sicut a peregrinis episcopis et transmarinis absoluto Caeciliano meruit damnari Donatus. damnatus est Maximianus cum duodecim ordinatoribus suis. factio quidem ipsa plurimos continebat; centum erant fortassis episcopi. sed ne maior praecisio fieret, isti noluerunt paucis deiectis multis imponere disciplinam. damnarunt solos qui affuerunt ordinationi Maximiani, quando contra episcopum suum illicite est leuatus episcopus; ceteri in ipsa factione constituti, si redire ad ecclesiam uellent, in suis permitterentur honoribus. uerbis quidem suis ostendebant eos foris esse ab ecclesia; quem enim hortaris ut intret, foris est. constituto ergo die, intra quem diem si redirent nihil eis obessent quae aduersus Primianum dicebantur, decreto Bagaiensi firmauerunt, damnatus est Maximianus cum duodecim. coepit agi, ut damnati de basilicis pellerentur. interpellantur iudices, interpellantur proconsules, in iudicium allegatur episcopale Bagaiense concilium. dicuntur haeretici, demonstrantur damnati, impetrantur iussiones, auxilia congregantur, uenitur ad eiciendos de basilicis homines damnatos et in sua pertinacia constitutos. illis condemnatis populi qui fauebant restiterunt, ubi non potuerunt uicti sunt, in locum eorum qui uicti sunt et expulsi alii ordinati sunt. ex quibus duos nouimus, ut de ceteris taceamus, unum Felicianum (Mustitanum), alterum Praetextatum Assuritanum, quos post annos duos aut tres per Optatum Gildonianum post multas illis illatas persecutiones iudiciariis prosecutionibus et tota acrimonia potestatum in suis honoribus susceperunt. post damnationem suam, post eiectionem, post persecutiones susceperunt illos in honoribus suis, adiunxerunt sibi socios atque collegas. nam in loco unius ipsorum Praetextati Assuritani alium iam ordinauerant nomine Rogatum, qui modo catholicus est, cui exercitus istorum, id est agmen circumcellionum, . linguam et manum praecidit. illi autem, qui per ipsum tempus, quo illi damnati foris erant, ferme per triennium baptizati sunt a damnatis, baptizati sunt foris ab ecclesia istorum, sic sunt suscepti. nemo dixit non habes baptismum, quia foris es baptizatus\': et rebaptizatur qui uenit de Epheso de Smyrna de Thessalonica de ceteris ecclesiis, quas suo labore apostoli plantauerunt et ad quas legimus missas apostolorum epistulas, quas audimus in ecclesia recitari.
thought_title: The Maximianist schism as a mirror of the Caecilian case
orientation: Augustine is narrating the recent Donatist schism of Maximianus against Primianus, showing how the Donatists treated their own schismatics differently from how they treated the Catholic Church over Caecilian.
pass_a_gloss: A certain Maximianus was a deacon of Carthage in the Donatist party. Whether by the merit of his pride or, as they themselves think, by the merit of his justice, he offended his bishop, that is Primianus of Carthage, whether unjustly, if a proud man offended a better man, or justly, if a good man offended a worse man. He was excommunicated by Primianus. He went to neighboring bishops, stirred up ill will against Primianus, accused him before them. They came to Carthage. The many Donatist bishops who came wanted Primianus to come to them, just as their ancestors wanted Caecilian to come to them. When the plot was discovered, Primianus refused to come to them, just as Caecilian refused to come to those others. Primianus was condemned by them in his absence, just as Caecilian was condemned by those others in his absence. What an image of things God willed to place before our eyes in recent time, since forgetfulness was already erasing things too ancient! He was condemned in his absence. By other bishops of the Donatist party Primianus was restored to communion, or rather, because they did not depose him, he was established in his own see. The Maximianists were condemned, just as Donatus deserved to be condemned after Caecilian was acquitted by foreign and overseas bishops. Maximianus was condemned with his twelve ordainers. The faction itself indeed contained very many; there were perhaps a hundred bishops. But lest a greater cutting off be made, they did not wish to impose discipline on many when a few had been cast down. They condemned only those who were present at the ordination of Maximianus, when a bishop was unlawfully raised up against his own bishop; the rest who remained in that faction, if they wished to return to the church, would be allowed to remain in their honors. By their words indeed they showed that those men were outside the church; for the one whom you urge to enter is outside. Therefore, when a day had been set, within which day if they returned nothing that was said against Primianus would harm them, they confirmed it by the decree of Bagai, Maximianus was condemned with the twelve. It began to be done, that the condemned men be driven from the basilicas. Judges are appealed to, proconsuls are appealed to, the episcopal council of Bagai is cited in court. They are called heretics, they are shown to be condemned, orders are obtained, forces are gathered, they come to eject from the basilicas men who were condemned and who remained in their own obstinacy. When those men had been condemned, the people who favored them resisted; where they could not prevail they were defeated, and in the place of those who were defeated and expelled others were ordained. Of whom we know two, to be silent about the rest, one Felicianus of Musti, the other Praetextatus of Assuras, whom after two or three years through Optatus the Gildonian, after many persecutions inflicted on them, by judicial prosecutions and the whole bitterness of the powers, they received back in their honors. After their condemnation, after their ejection, after persecutions, they received them in their honors, they joined them to themselves as partners and colleagues. For in the place of one of them, Praetextatus of Assuras, they had already ordained another named Rogatus, who is now a Catholic, whose tongue and hand the army of those men, that is the band of Circumcellions, cut off. But those who during that time, while those condemned men were outside, were baptized by the condemned men for nearly three years, were baptized outside the church of those men, and were received in this way. No one said 'you do not have baptism, because you were baptized outside'; and yet one who comes from Ephesus, from Smyrna, from Thessalonica, from the other churches, which the apostles planted by their own labor and to which we read that the letters of the apostles were sent, which we hear recited in church, is rebaptized.

pass_b_english: There was a certain deacon in Carthage named Maximianus, in the Donatist party. Whether deservedly for his pride or, as they think, deservedly for his righteousness, he offended his bishop—that is, Primianus of Carthage—either unjustly, if he was a proud man against a better one, or justly, if he was an upright man against a worse one. He was excommunicated by Primianus. He went to the neighboring bishops, stirred up resentment against Primianus, and accused him before them. They came to Carthage. Many Donatist bishops who had come wanted Primianus to come to them, just as their predecessors wanted Caecilian to come to them. When the faction became known, Primianus refused to come to them, just as Caecilian refused to come to those earlier ones. Primianus was condemned by them in his absence, just as Caecilian was condemned by those earlier ones in his absence. What a picture of events God chose to place before our eyes in recent times, because forgetfulness was already erasing things too ancient! He was condemned in his absence. Primianus was restored to communion by other bishops of the Donatist party—or rather, because they had not deposed him, he was confirmed in his own see. The Maximianists were condemned, just as Donatus deserved condemnation when Caecilian had been acquitted by foreign and overseas bishops. Maximianus was condemned along with the twelve who ordained him. The faction itself contained many people; there were perhaps a hundred bishops. But so that no greater split would occur, these men refused, with a few cast down, to impose discipline on the many. They condemned only those who were present at Maximianus's ordination, when a bishop was unlawfully elevated against their own bishop. The rest who remained in that faction, if they wished to return to the church, were to be allowed to keep their honors. By their own words they showed that those people were outside the church; for the one you urge to enter is outside. So a day was set, within which if they returned, nothing that was said against Primianus would harm them, and they confirmed it by the decree of Bagai. Maximianus was condemned along with the twelve. Then action began to be taken to drive the condemned men from their basilicas. Judges were petitioned, proconsuls were petitioned, the episcopal council of Bagai was cited in court. They were called heretics, they were shown to be condemned, orders were obtained, forces were gathered, and they came to eject from the basilicas men who were condemned and fixed in their stubbornness. The people who favored those condemned men supported them; where they could not resist they were defeated, and in place of those defeated and expelled others were ordained. Of these we know two—to say nothing of the rest—one Felicianus of Musti, the other Praetextatus of Assuras. After two or three years, through Optatus the Gildonian, after many persecutions had been inflicted on them through judicial prosecutions and the full harshness of the authorities, they received them back in their honors. After their condemnation, after their expulsion, after persecutions, they received them in their honors as partners and colleagues. For in the place of one of them, Praetextatus of Assuras, they had already ordained another man named Rogatus, who is now a Catholic, whose tongue and hand the army of those people—that is, the band of Circumcellions—cut off. But those who were baptized by the condemned men during the time when those men were outside, for nearly three years, were baptized outside the church of those men, and they were received in this way. No one said, 'You do not have baptism, because you were baptized outside.' And yet a person who comes from Ephesus, from Smyrna, from Thessalonica, from the other churches that the apostles planted by their labor and to which we read that the apostles' letters were sent, which we hear read in church—that person is rebaptized.

problems.quote: just as Donatus deserved to be condemned after Caecilian was acquitted by foreign and overseas bishops
problems.source_quote: sicut a peregrinis episcopis et transmarinis absoluto Caeciliano meruit damnari Donatus
problems.why: meruit damnari = 'deserved to be condemned' but the construction is passive; Donatus is subject, but 'meruit' implies he got his due
problems.fix: just as Donatus deserved condemnation when Caecilian was acquitted by foreign and overseas bishops

problems.quote: when a bishop was illicitly raised up against his own bishop
problems.source_quote: quando contra episcopum suum illicite est leuatus episcopus
problems.why: illicitly = 'unlawfully', but leuatus = 'elevated/raised to office'; 'his own bishop' refers to Primianus as the bishop of the one ordained
problems.fix: when a bishop was unlawfully elevated against his own bishop

problems.quote: and they confirmed this by the decree of Bagai
problems.why: firmauerunt = 'they confirmed/strengthened' with ablative; 'by the decree' is right but 'this' is added
problems.fix: they confirmed it by the Bagaiense decree

problems.quote: were baptized outside their church, and they were received in this way
problems.source_quote: baptizati sunt foris ab ecclesia istorum, sic sunt suscepti
problems.why: ab ecclesia istorum = 'by their church' (the Donatist church); 'outside their church' misrepresents agency
problems.fix: were baptized outside by their church, and were received thus

problems.why: 'Plot' is wrong for 'factione'; it means the faction/schism became known, not a plot.
problems.ruling: 'Factione' means 'faction/party,' not secret plot; context shows schism known, not conspiracy discovered.

problems.why: 'Ordinatores' are those he ordained, not those who ordained him; he raised up twelve bishops.
problems.ruling: 'Ordinatoribus' = those who ordained him (ablative with 'damnatus est'); 'suis' refers to Maximianus's bishops, not his own ordainers.

problems.quote: The people who favored those condemned men resisted; where they could not prevail, they were defeated
problems.source_quote: illis condemnatis populi qui fauebant restiterunt, ubi non potuerunt uicti sunt
problems.why: Latin means 'when those condemned men could not hold out, they were defeated'; 'populi' is dative, not nominative subject.
problems.fix: the people who favored those condemned men supported them; where they could not hold out, they were defeated
problems.ruling: 'Populi' is genitive/dative; 'illis condemnatis' is ablative absolute; 'ubi non potuerunt' refers to condemned men, not people.

problems.quote: they received them in their honors and joined them to themselves as partners and colleagues
problems.source_quote: susciperunt illos in honoribus suis, adiunxerunt sibi socios atque collegas
problems.why: 'Socios atque collegas' is accusative: they received them as partners and colleagues, not 'joined them to themselves as'.
problems.fix: they received them in their honors as partners and colleagues
problems.ruling: 'Socios atque collegas' is accusative in apposition to 'illos': received them as partners, not joined them as.

problems.quote: through the fault of his own pride or, as they think, through the fault of his own righteousness
problems.source_quote: siue merito superbiae suae siue, ut ipsi putant, merito iustitiae suae
problems.why: merito = 'deservedly'/'justly', not 'through the fault'; 'fault' contradicts iustitiae
problems.fix: whether deservedly for his pride or, as they think, deservedly for his righteousness
problems.ruling: merito = 'deservedly'; 'through the fault' contradicts merito iustitiae suae, 'deservedly for his righteousness'

edits.old: Whether through the fault of his own pride or, as they think, through the fault of his own righteousness
edits.new: Whether deservedly for his pride or, as they think, deservedly for his righteousness

edits.old: just as Donatus deserved to be condemned after Caecilian was acquitted by foreign and overseas bishops
edits.new: just as Donatus deserved condemnation when Caecilian was acquitted by foreign and overseas bishops

edits.old: Maximianus was condemned along with his twelve ordainers
edits.new: Maximianus was condemned along with the twelve he ordained

edits.old: when a bishop was illicitly raised up against his own bishop
edits.new: when a bishop was unlawfully elevated against his own bishop

edits.old: and they confirmed this by the decree of Bagai
edits.new: and they confirmed it by the decree of Bagai

edits.old: The people who favored those condemned men resisted; where they could not prevail, they were defeated
edits.new: The people who favored those condemned men supported them; where they could not hold out, they were defeated

edits.old: they received them in their honors and joined them to themselves as partners and colleagues
edits.new: they received them in their honors as partners and colleagues

edits.old: were baptized outside their church, and they were received in this way
edits.new: were baptized outside by their church, and they were received in this way

fixed: merito superbiae suae / merito iustitiae suae: 'deservedly' not 'through the fault'; edited.
meruit damnari Donatus: passive construction; edited to 'deserved condemnation'.
duodecim ordinatoribus suis: 'the twelve he ordained' not 'his twelve ordainers'; edited.
illicite est leuatus episcopus: 'unlawfully elevated' not 'illicitly raised up'; edited.
decreto Bagaiensi firmauerunt: 'confirmed it' not 'confirmed this'; edited.
populi qui fauebant restiterunt, ubi non potuerunt uicti sunt: 'supported them' and 'they could not hold out'; edited.
susceperunt illos in honoribus suis, adiunxerunt sibi socios atque collegas: 'received them as partners and colleagues'; edited.
baptizati sunt foris ab ecclesia istorum: 'baptized outside by their church'; edited.

problems.quote: just as Donatus deserved condemnation when Caecilian was acquitted by foreign and overseas bishops
problems.source_quote: sicut a peregrinis episcopis et transmarinis absoluto Caeciliano meruit damnari Donatus
problems.why: Latin has Donatus deserving condemnation, not Caecilian being acquitted by those bishops; 'absoluto Caeciliano' is ablative absolute ('when Caecilian had been acquitted'), not 'by foreign and overseas bishops' modifying acquittal.
problems.fix: just as Donatus deserved condemnation when Caecilian had been acquitted by foreign and overseas bishops

problems.quote: they were defeated, and in the place of those who were defeated and expelled, others were ordained
problems.source_quote: ubi non potuerunt uicti sunt, in locum eorum qui uicti sunt et expulsi alii ordinati sunt
problems.why: The first 'uicti sunt' refers to the condemned men's supporters being defeated, but 'ubi non potuerunt' means 'where they could not' [hold out/resist], not 'where they could not hold out, they were defeated'—the syntax is compressed but the supporters were defeated where they couldn't resist.
problems.fix: where they could not resist they were defeated, and in place of those defeated and expelled others were ordained

problems.quote: Maximianus was condemned along with the twelve he ordained.
problems.source_quote: damnatus est Maximianus cum duodecim ordinatoribus suis.
problems.why: ordinatoribus means 'those who ordained him,' not 'those he ordained.' The twelve ordained Maximianus, not vice versa.
problems.fix: Maximianus was condemned along with the twelve who ordained him.
problems.ruling: ordinatoribus suis = 'his ordainers,' not 'those he ordained.' Maximianus was ordained by twelve bishops, not vice versa.

edits.old: just as Donatus deserved condemnation when Caecilian was acquitted by foreign and overseas bishops
edits.new: just as Donatus deserved condemnation when Caecilian had been acquitted by foreign and overseas bishops

edits.old: where they could not hold out, they were defeated, and in the place of those who were defeated and expelled, others were ordained
edits.new: where they could not resist they were defeated, and in place of those defeated and expelled others were ordained

edits.old: Maximianus was condemned along with the twelve he ordained.
edits.new: Maximianus was condemned along with the twelve who ordained him.

fixed: Added 'had been' to clarify the ablative absolute 'absoluto Caeciliano' (when Caecilian had been acquitted).
Changed 'where they could not hold out, they were defeated' to 'where they could not resist they were defeated' to reflect 'ubi non potuerunt uicti sunt'.
Changed 'the twelve he ordained' to 'the twelve who ordained him' to correct 'duodecim ordinatoribus suis' (his twelve ordainers).

problems.quote: they did not want to impose discipline on the many by casting down a few
problems.source_quote: isti noluerunt paucis deiectis multis imponere disciplinam
problems.why: Subject is 'isti' (the Donatist bishops condemning), not 'they' ambiguous; 'deiectis' is ablative absolute 'with a few cast down,' not 'by casting down.'
problems.fix: these men refused, with a few cast down, to impose discipline on the many

problems.quote: when a bishop was unlawfully elevated against his own bishop
problems.source_quote: quando contra episcopum suum illicite est leuatus episcopus
problems.why: 'episcopum suum' means 'their own bishop' (Primianus, the bishop of the ordainers), not 'his own bishop.'
problems.fix: when a bishop was unlawfully elevated against their own bishop

problems.quote: were baptized outside by their church
problems.source_quote: baptizati sunt foris ab ecclesia istorum
problems.why: 'istorum' = 'of those men' (the condemned Maximianists), not 'their church' in sense of the Donatist church generally; it was the condemned men's church.
problems.fix: were baptized outside by the church of those men

problems.why: Source has lacuna/dot before 'linguam'; English silently supplies without marking textual gap. The source is damaged here.
problems.fix: [...] cut off his tongue and hand
problems.ruling: Source has lacuna marked by dot before 'linguam'; English silently supplies 'tongue and hand' without noting textual gap.

edits.old: they did not want to impose discipline on the many by casting down a few
edits.new: these men refused, with a few cast down, to impose discipline on the many

edits.old: when a bishop was unlawfully elevated against his own bishop
edits.new: when a bishop was unlawfully elevated against their own bishop

edits.old: were baptized outside by their church
edits.new: were baptized outside by the church of those men
[...] cut off his tongue and hand.

fixed: Source 'isti noluerunt paucis deiectis multis imponere disciplinam': subject is 'isti' (these men, the Donatist bishops), and 'paucis deiectis' is ablative absolute 'with a few cast down'; English 'they did not want...by casting down' misread the construction.
Source 'contra episcopum suum': 'suum' refers to the ordainers' own bishop (Primianus), not the bishop being elevated; English 'his own bishop' misstates the referent.
Source 'ab ecclesia istorum': 'istorum' refers to the condemned Maximianists, not the Donatist church generally; English 'their church' is ambiguous and misleading.
Source has a lacuna before 'linguam et manum praecidit'; English silently supplied 'cut off' without marking the gap. Inserted '[...]' and made the object explicit.

fixed.quote: and whose tongue and hand the army of those people—that is, the band of Circumcellions—[...] cut off his tongue and hand
fixed.fix: whose tongue and hand the army of those people—that is, the band of Circumcellions—cut off
fixed.note: The English states the object twice ('whose tongue and hand ... cut off his tongue and hand') around a stray [...], so the clause is ungrammatical; the Latin gives the object once.

fixed.quote: were baptized outside by the church of those men
fixed.fix: were baptized outside the church of those men
fixed.note: 'Foris ab ecclesia istorum' means outside their church (compare 'foris esse ab ecclesia' earlier); 'by the church' wrongly makes the church the agent.

dismissed.quote: And yet a person who comes from Ephesus
dismissed.why: Source says 'and the one who comes from Ephesus...is rebaptized'—the 'et' connects to the previous sentence, not 'and yet.' The rebaptism is presented as parallel, not contrastive.
dismissed.note: The context sets two cases against each other, so this 'et' carries the sense 'and yet'; the English is a fair rendering.
